actOfContrition.title: Act of Contrition
body: O my God, I am heartily sorry for having offended Thee, and I detest all my sins because of Thy just punishments, but most of all because they offend Thee, my God, Who art all-good and deserving of all my love. I firmly resolve, with the help of Thy grace, to sin no more and to avoid the near occasions of sin. Amen.

guideIntro: This guide describes what usually happens in individual confession and what to say. Details vary from parish to parish and priest to priest. If anything differs, follow the priest.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Take a few minutes beforehand to recall your sins since your last confession. This app does not include an examination of conscience; many parishes provide one, and printed and online versions are widely available.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Know roughly how long it has been since your last confession. The Confessions tab shows this.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: You may confess anonymously behind a screen or face to face. Either is acceptable. Choose whichever you prefer when you enter.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Enter when the light or door indicates the confessional is free. Kneel or sit. The priest may greet you first.

lines.speaker: both
lines.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: The priest may briefly invite you to trust in God's mercy, and may read a short passage from Scripture. When he finishes his invitation, answer:

lines.speaker: penitent
lines.text: Amen.

lines.speaker: penitent
lines.text: {blessMe}

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: If this is your first confession, say: This is my first confession.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: You may briefly mention your state in life if it helps the priest, for example: I am married, or, I am a student. This is optional.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: State your sins plainly. For serious (mortal) sins, give the kind of sin and, as best you can, how many times. Less serious (venial) sins may also be confessed. There is no need for long explanations unless the priest asks.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: If you forget a sin, it is still forgiven when you receive absolution in good faith. Mention it at your next confession if you remember it.

lines.speaker: penitent
lines.text: For these and all my sins, I am truly sorry.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: The priest may offer brief advice and then assigns a penance, usually a prayer or a small act.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: If you did not understand or hear the penance, ask the priest to repeat it.

lines.speaker: penitent
lines.text: Thank you, Father.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: The priest invites you to express your sorrow, often by asking you to make your Act of Contrition.

lines.speaker: penitent
lines.text: {actOfContrition}

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: You may read the prayer from this screen; the Prayer tab shows the same text. If you don't know it, you can also ask the priest to help you.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: The priest extends his hand and prays the prayer of absolution. It ends with the words: in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Answer:

lines.speaker: penitent
lines.text: Amen.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good.

lines.speaker: penitent
lines.text: His mercy endures for ever.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: The priest then dismisses you, usually telling you that your sins are forgiven and to go in peace. You may answer:

lines.speaker: penitent
lines.text: Thanks be to God.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Some priests shorten the dismissal. A simple "Thank you, Father" as you leave is always appropriate.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Spend a few moments in prayer.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Complete your penance as soon as you reasonably can.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Log this confession so you know the date next time.
